title: OwnMem procedure replay record
description:
One replay of one exact procedure version, written down so someone else can re-check it. This is the artefact `kind: replay` evidence points at, and it exists because the evidence kind previously had nothing behind it: a replay anchor was verified as if it were an ordinary code path, which proved a file existed and said nothing about whether anything had been replayed. The three things that were missing are the three things required here -- the fixture it ran against and its content hash, the environment it ran in, and which of the procedure's declared postconditions were checked and how they came out.

An environment naming production or release is representable on purpose. A record that honestly says where it ran can be refused by the verifier; a schema that made the sentence unsayable would only ensure the run was never written down.

replay_id.description: Identity of this replay, echoed by the evidence locator. The verifier refuses a mismatch: without it a receipt could name one replay and be checked against another.

procedure.description: The exact procedure that was replayed, bound to its bytes. Editing a step after the replay makes the record describe something that no longer exists, and the verifier treats that as blocking rather than drift: an unrelated refactor cannot touch a procedure file, and the playbook a reader is shown must be the one that was actually replayed.

fixture.description: The input it ran against. Recorded here as well as in the procedure because a procedure may be replayed against a failure sample, and the record has to say which input this run used.

environment.description: Where it ran, in the two dimensions that can change what a replay does and are not the identity of a machine. The components are stored next to the digest so a mismatch can say which one moved instead of only that something did.

fingerprint.description: Digest of the two components above and nothing else. Deliberately excludes every dimension that identifies a machine, a user or a checkout location -- absolute paths, home directory, user name, host name, machine id, cpu count, total memory, architecture, the current commit, locale and time zone -- because evidence in this repository has to stay valid across changing computers, user names and repository paths, and a fingerprint holding any of those would invalidate itself the first time the work moved.

postconditions_checked.description: Which of the procedure's declared postconditions this run actually decided, and what came out. Non-empty: a replay that checked nothing has demonstrated nothing, and would otherwise be the cheapest way to manufacture an unlocked promotion. Every id is checked against the procedure's own declarations, so a run cannot claim a postcondition the procedure never made.

outcome.description: Two words, no third. 'Not checked' is expressed by not appearing in this list, and an inconclusive check is a failed one: a replay that could not decide has not decided in favour.

failure_samples_checked.description: Which declared failure samples this run replayed. May be empty -- a run that only exercised the happy path says so by leaving this empty rather than by omitting the field -- but any id in it has to be one the procedure declares.

outcome.description: unexpected_success is the interesting one: the procedure did the thing on an input it was supposed to refuse, which is a regression no happy-path replay can see.
